Each identity must maintain a rolling record of inter-arrival intervals; the system scores variance against a quill-thin tolerance band and rejects registrations whose timing is too regular. New identities inherit the median cadence of the subnet they join, so a farm spinning up many agents at once produces a marble-smooth traffic curve that flags instantly. Attacker cost: idle each clone through randomized, human-plausible gaps for weeks, or lose the tundra of wasted compute.
